rv.q: Jackson's jazz-soaked, somewhat 'Enron'-tinged production is a hoot from start to finish.
After a much-praised run at Stratford, the RSC's best piece of new writing in years settles triumphantly into its London berth.
Heffernan's performance is superb: affable and charismatic yet slightly aloof, as the play wears on he retreats further into his core, his stare increasingly distant.

Some odd touches – the very literal representation of the Little Boy bomb, a couple of overly caricatured portrayals – as well as a malfunctioning speaker during Heffernan's emotional climactic address on press night, did little to detract from a deeply thought-provoking, compelling and important new work.

cn.t: An ambitious three-hour epic about the father of the atomic bomb earns acclaim for its scope, stylish direction, and strong performances, proving intellectually demanding theatre can thrive in the West End.
